Furthermore, we introduce a transformation to adjust a given push-sum scheme in a way that the bound on the rate provably improves -- and often so does the true convergence rate. Theoretical understanding is complemented by numerical results, where the quality of all three directions is demonstrated: for the bound on the rate, for the computational complexity and for the improvement strategy.
item.dc:creator: Bal\'azs Gerencs\'er, Mikl\'os Kornyik

item.title: Probabilistic well-posedness of dispersive PDEs beyond variance blowup II: quadratic nonlinear wave equation
item.description: arXiv:2611.30936v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study the quadratic nonlinear wave equation (NLW), posed on the two-dimensional torus, with rough Gaussian random initial data beyond the variance blowup threshold observed by Okamoto and the fourth author (2021). By introducing a suitable vanishing multiplicative renormalization constant on the frequency-truncated Gaussian random initial data, we prove that the corresponding solutions converge in law to a solution to the stochastic NLW with zero initial data, driven by a Gaussian space-time noise whose temporal covariance at each spatial Fourier mode is given by the Bessel function of order $0$. We also show that the solution to the limiting equation almost surely blows up in a finite time, and that the convergence above holds on every compact time interval before the maximal existence time. %on the maximal time of existence. A main new ingredient is the analysis of the oscillatory covariance of the second Picard iterates. We identify the limiting covariance by averaging the leading oscillatory phase over the angular variable. In contrast to our previous work on the Benjamin-Bona-Mahony equation (2025), multilinear dispersive smoothing plays an essential role both in proving tightness of the second Picard iterates and in controlling the rough nonlinear interactions via paracontrolled analysis. The resulting gain of a quarter of a derivative persists in the limit, where it is reflected in the decay of the Bessel covariance.
item.dc:creator: Guopeng Li, Jiawei Li, Shao Liu, Tadahiro Oh, Nikolay Tzvetkov

item.title: Revealing Geometry under Strong Noise: Spectral Embeddings and Clustering via Random Geometric Graphs
item.description: arXiv:2611.31047v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Modern massive datasets often contain useful low-dimensional nonlinear structures that are hidden by noise. Spectral embedding algorithms rely on meaningful local relationships between observations, but noise accumulated across many coordinates can make the observed distances unreliable. This also complicates clustering when groups have curved or concentric shapes and cannot be distinguished by their centers. In this paper, we develop a new method that denoises pairwise distances before using them to construct spectral embeddings and identify communities. Our approach uses cross-fitted projections to estimate distances between the underlying signals, selects a neighborhood radius from the observed sample, and builds a random geometric graph whose spectral coordinates represent the latent geometric structure. By connecting nearby points, such a geometric graph can distinguish different groups even when their centers coincide. A novel recursive procedure is then proposed to extract clusters from the graph using its spectral embeddings when such clusters exist. On the theoretical side, under a manifold model, we provide guarantees for our spectral embedding algorithm, which can be understood through the eigendecomposition of an integral operator associated with the underlying geometry. We show that the algorithm is robust to noise when the total noise energy is comparable to the total signal energy or, under additional conditions, exceeds it. To our knowledge, this is among the first spectral embedding algorithms that can handle such strong noise in datasets with nonlinear structures. In addition, our proposed clustering algorithm can recover the underlying clusters even when their centers coincide. Numerical studies demonstrate the superior performance of the proposed method in mitigating noise and revealing geometric structures for both spectral embedding and clustering.
item.dc:creator: Hai-Xiao Wang, Xiucai Ding

item.title: Matching Under Metric Privacy
item.description: arXiv:2611.31208v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study how to represent and randomize points in $d$-dimensional Euclidean space to obtain accurate bipartite matchings under metric privacy. Given $n$ private and $n$ public points, we analyze local mechanisms that randomize each private point or its distances to the public points. Using the public points' affine span, we construct a smaller representation that preserves all matching costs. When a trusted server receives the private points, we establish privacy and utility guarantees for Gumbel matching, which randomizes edge costs and releases only the assignment. Through upper bounds and worst-case constructions, we establish the tight rate $\Theta\!\left(n\min\{d,\log n\}/\varepsilon\right)$ for expected cost above the nonprivate optimum. Benchmark experiments support $d\approx\log n$ as a practical guide to the transition between directly randomizing point coordinates and using Gumbel matching. Extensions to squared Euclidean costs enable private nonparametric two-sample hypothesis testing. These results show how the application's trust model guides representation and dimension choices for better utility: under local privacy, low-dimensional point representations reduce excess cost, while under central privacy, distance representations achieve the optimal rate even in high dimension.
item.dc:creator: Hongyi B. Hu, Dung Nguyen, M. Amin Rahimian

item.title: Central limit theorem for energies of determinantal point processes on complex manifolds I
item.description: arXiv:2611.31229v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study the Bergman determinantal point process associated with a positive line bundle on a compact Riemann surface. Consider the U-statistic given by the Green function, called the Green energy. For a configuration of $N$ points, the expectation of Green energy is $\frac12 N\log N+O(N)$, and the variance is $(\log 2-\pi^2/24)N+O(\log^2 N)$. We prove a central limit theorem for the Green energy by combining local Bergman kernel asymptotics with an expansion for the cumulants. A central limit theorem also holds for the logarithmic energy of Bergman determinantal point process on complex manifolds.
item.dc:creator: Hao Wu

item.title: Dirichlet heat kernel estimates for fractional Laplacian under non-local perturbation
item.description: arXiv:1503.05302v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: For $d\geq 1$ and $0<\beta<\alpha<2$, consider a family of non-local operators $$\mathcal{S}^{b}f(x):=\lim_{\varepsilon\to 0}\mathcal{A}(d,-\beta)\int_{ \{z\in \mathbb{R}^d: |z|>\varepsilon\}}(f(x+z)-f(x))\frac{b(x,z)}{|z|^{d+\beta}}\,{\mathrm{d}z},$$ and $b(x,z)$ is a bounded measurable function on $\mathbb{R}^{d}\times\mathbb{R}^{d}$ with $b(x,z)=b(x,-z)$ for every $x,z\in\mathbb{R}^{d}$. Here ${\mathcal{A}}(d, -\beta)$ is the normalizing constant for which $\mathcal{S}^b=-(-\Delta)^{\beta/2}$ when $b(x, z)\equiv 1$. It is known that if $b(x, z) \geq -\frac{{\mathcal{A}}(d, -\alpha)} {{\mathcal{A}}(d, -\beta)}\, |z|^{\beta -\alpha}$ for a.e. $z\in\mathbb{R}^{d}$, then $\mathcal{L}^b$ admits a unique fundamental solution $p^{b}(t,x,y)$, which determines a conservative Feller process $X^{b}$ with the strong Feller property. In this paper, we study the subprocess $X^{b,D}$ of $X^{b}$ killed upon leaving a $C^{1,1}$ open set $D\subset \mathbb{R}^d$. We establish explicit small-time upper and lower bounds for its transition density function $p^{b}_{D}(t,x,y)$. These estimates are uniform in $b$: all constants depend on $b$ only through an upper bound of $\|b\|_{\infty}$. Moreover, $b$ enters the form of the upper bound only through the size of its large positive part, $\mathrm{ess\,sup}_{x\in\mathbb{R}^{d},\,|z|>\lambda}b(x,z)^{+}$ for a fixed $\lambda>0$. When the jump kernel of $\mathcal{L}^b$ satisfies matching upper and lower bounds, either of $\alpha$-stable type or of mixed $\alpha$- and $\beta$-stable type, the small-time estimates for $p^{b}_{D}(t,x,y)$ are sharp. For bounded $D$, we also obtain large-time estimates governed by the principal eigenvalue of the generator of $X^{b,D}$. Under a non-degeneracy condition on the jump kernel, we further establish sharp two-sided estimates on the Green function of $X^{b, D}$ in bounded $C^{1,1}$ open sets.
item.dc:creator: Zhen-Qing Chen, Ting Yang

item.title: Ruin Theory Problems in Simple SDE Models with Large Deviation Asymptotics
item.description: arXiv:2312.08165v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We examine hitting probability problems for Ornstein-Uhlenbeck (OU) processes and Geometric Brownian motions (GBM) with respect to exponential boundaries related to problems arising in risk theory and asset and liability models in pension funds. In Section 2 we consider the OU process described by the Stochastic Differential Equation (SDE) $dX_t = \mu X_t dt + \sigma dW_t$ with $X_0=x_0$ evolving between a lower and an upper deterministic exponential boundary. Both the finite horizon ``ruin probability'' problem and the corresponding infinite horizon problem is examined in the low noise case, using the Wentzell-Freidlin approach in order to obtain logarithmic asymptotics for the probability of hitting either the lower or the upper boundary. The resulting variational problems are studied in detail. The exponential rate characterizing the ruin probability and the ``path to ruin'' are obtained by their solution. Logarithmic asymptotics for the meeting probability in a pair of OU processes with different positive drift coefficients, driven by independent Brownian motions is also obtained using Wentzell-Freidlin techniques. The optimal paths followed by the two processes and the meeting time $T$ are determined by solving a variational problem with transversality conditions. In Section 3 a corresponding problem involving a Geometric Brownian motion is considered. Since in this case, an exact, closed form solution is also available and we take advantage of this situation in order to explore numerically the quality of the Large Deviations results obtained using the Wentzell-Freidlin approach.
item.arxiv:journal_reference: Journal of Computational and Applied Mathematics, vol. 477, 2026
item.dc:creator: Efstathia Bougioukli, Michael A. Zazanis

item.title: Functional weak convergence of stochastic integrals for moving averages and continuous-time random walks
item.description: arXiv:2401.13543v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: There is an extensive theory of weak convergence for moving averages and continuous-time random walks (CTRWs) with respect to Skorokhod's M1 and J1 topologies. Here we address the fundamental question of how this translates into functional limit theorems in the M1 or J1 topology for stochastic integrals driven by these processes. As an important application, we provide weak approximation results for general SDEs driven by time-changed L\'evy processes. Such SDEs and their associated fractional Fokker--Planck--Kolmogorov equations are central to models of anomalous diffusion in statistical physics. Our results yield a rigorous functional characterisation of these as continuum limits of the underlying models driven by CTRWs. With regard to strictly M1 convergent moving averages and correlated CTRWs, it turns out that the convergence of stochastic integrals can fail decidedly and fundamental new challenges arise compared to the J1 setting. Nevertheless, we identify natural classes of integrand processes for which there is M1 convergence of the stochastic integrals. We also show that these results are flexible enough to yield functional limit theorems in the M1 topology for certain stochastic delay differential equations driven by moving averages.
item.dc:creator: Andreas S{\o}jmark, Fabrice Wunderlich

item.title: Lyapunov exponents for products of truncated orthogonal matrices
item.description: arXiv:2505.04928v5 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study the Lyapunov exponents for products of $N$ independent truncated Haar orthogonal matrices of size $n$. We prove that, in principle, provided that $N/n \to \infty$ , the first $k$ Lyapunov exponents are approximately independent and Gaussian in a non-asymptotic sense, where $k$ may depend on $N$ and $n$.
item.dc:creator: Dong Qichao

item.title: Necessary and sufficient conditions for high dimensional Central Limit Theorem under moment conditions
item.description: arXiv:2512.22312v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We characterize the dimension growth rate in the high dimensional central limit theorems (or CLTs) over hyper-rectangles. First, we find out the moment conditions that are both necessary and sufficient under the independence of the components. We consider four exhaustive classes, viz. when underlying random variables (I) have all polynomial moments, (II) have some polynomial moment of order higher than two, (III) have only second moment but no polynomial moment higher than two exists, and (IV) have infinite second moment, but belong to the domain of attraction of normal distribution. Next, we extend the sufficiency of the moment conditions in the Gaussian approximations of each of the aforementioned classes with same moment assumptions when the coordinates are dependent. For sub-Weibull marginals in Class (I), with $0<\alpha\le1/6$, strong non-degeneracy yields the optimal range $\log p=o(n^{2\alpha})$ which matches the rate obtained under coordinate-wise independence. However under marginal non-degeneracy, a Berry--Esseen bound gives the exponent $2\alpha/(1+4\alpha)$ up to logarithmic factors, and a counterexample proves that this exponent is optimal under marginal non-degeneracy. Under marginal non-degeneracy, Class (II) admits polynomial dimension growth up to logarithmic factors, while in Class (III) the marginal tails determine a growth rate, both of which again match with that when the coordinates are independent. In Class (IV), coordinate-wise normalization by truncated second moments yields a high dimensioonal CLT under additional tail and covariance conditions. Thus, we derive necessary and sufficient moment conditions for the validity of the CLT over hyper-rectangles in high dimensions in all possible regimes, showing that the CLT may hold under much weaker conditions compared to those present in the existing literature.
item.dc:creator: Debraj Das, Soumendra Lahiri

item.title: An Alternative Proof of an Erd\H os-R\'enyi Law for the Longest Consecutive Monotone Block in a Random Permutation
item.description: arXiv:2602.18970v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: $\{X_j\}_{j=1}^\infty$ of i.i.d.~($p$) coin-tosses, the longest run $L_n$ of heads in the first $n$ coin tosses approaches $\log_{1/p}n$ almost surely. In this paper we explore a formulation of this result in the case of random permutations and prove an Erd\H os-R\'enyi law for the longest consecutive monotone block in a random permutation. This problem has been studied before by several authors, and we offer a Poisson approximation viewpoint on this issue using the Stein-Chen method.
item.dc:creator: Anusha Asthana, Anant Godbole

item.title: Pathwise stability of Wasserstein contractive Markov chain Monte Carlo
item.description: arXiv:2602.19119v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study pathwise behaviour of Markov chain Monte Carlo (MCMC) algorithms. For chains satisfying a contraction assumption w.r.t. a Wasserstein distance we establish explicit deterministic rates that hold for single realisations on sets of high probability. Additionally, we show that the median of means estimator further increases the pathwise stability. To prove our main results we employ a well-known martingale decomposition technique based on solutions of Poisson's equation. Finally, we apply our results to concrete MCMC methods including the No-U-Turn-Sampler, the Metropolis adjusted Langevin algorithm and slice samplers.
item.dc:creator: Julian Hofstadler

item.title: Spectral Properties of Dense Barab\'asi-Albert Graphs
item.description: arXiv:2606.20816v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Preferential attachment graphs model networks whose growth produces highly uneven degree distributions, describing many real-world systems. Their adjacency spectra are important because they allow graph-theoretic questions to be studied through the eigenvalues of matrices. We analyze the adjacency matrix of a dense Barab\'asi-Albert (B-A) multigraph, where the number of edges added at each step is proportional to the final number of vertices. First, we compute the large-$n$ limit of the expected adjacency matrix and show that it is described by a rank-one limiting kernel, viewed as a continuous analogue of the adjacency matrix. After centering and scaling, the fluctuations form a random matrix with a computable variance profile. Using the quadratic vector equation approach, we derive the limiting bulk spectral distribution. We also determine the asymptotic location of the leading eigenvalue generated by the rank-one mean component.
item.dc:creator: Steven J. Miller, Arman Rysmakhanov

item.title: Propagation of chaos for Belavkin equations beyond pure states
item.description: arXiv:2606.29557v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We establish quantitative trace-norm propagation of chaos for finite-dimensional quantum mean-field systems governed by Belavkin equations under continuous diffusive measurements. Our results concern random reduced states conditioned on the observation records of the entire particle system, rather than states averaged over these records. We allow arbitrary one-particle density matrices, general measurement operators, and both perfect and inefficient detection. Two regimes of initial data are considered. For initial states approaching a tensor product in trace norm, without requiring permutation invariance, we establish explicit convergence rates, improved from an inverse fourth-root to an inverse square-root rate when the one-particle initial state is faithful. More importantly, for permutation-invariant initial states, convergence of the two-particle marginal to a product suffices for propagation of chaos, even when the full initial state remains far from a tensor product. Quantitative convergence rates are obtained in this setting, including a sharper estimate under faithfulness. Our proofs combine purification, fully observed dilation, and uniform stability of linear Zakai equations with a relative-entropy method for the joint observation law and conditional quantum state. The latter controls the interacting dynamics through entropy-production estimates and extends to arbitrary-rank initial states by regularizing only the reference dynamics. These results provide a rigorous foundation for low-dimensional approximations of continuously monitored interacting quantum systems, including those with initially correlated states.
item.dc:creator: Gaoyue Guo

item.title: Coupling and Maximal Inequalities for Graph-Dependent Empirical Processes
item.description: arXiv:2606.31936v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We develop maximal inequalities for empirical processes indexed by graph-dependent observations. Our bounds separate the complexity of the indexing class from two features specific to graph dependence: the geometry of the underlying graph and the cost of coupling graph-separated blocks to independent copies. The coupling construction combines a novel graph-adapted dependence coefficient with a coloring of a block partition. As an application, we derive Glivenko--Cantelli results and characterize the associated effective sample size. A central implication is that graph-dependent empirical processes need not exhibit a generic root-$n$ rate: convergence is jointly determined by function-class complexity, graph geometry, and the decay of dependence with graph distance. We specialize the results to graphs with polynomial and exponential growth and to directed dyadic graphs. Finally, we apply the results to network autoregressive models, nonlinear local-propagation models, and treatment-interference settings.
item.dc:creator: Mengsi Gao, Demian Pouzo

item.title: Non-vanishing uniqueness threshold for hyperbolic Poisson-Voronoi percolation in dimension at least three
item.description: arXiv:2607.17764v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study the threshold for the existence of exactly one unbounded cluster for Poisson-Voronoi percolation on the $d$-dimensional hyperbolic space $\mathbb{H}^d$ for $d\geq 3$. By recent results of Greb\'ik and Recke and d'Achille et al., this "uniqueness threshold" $p_u(\lambda)$ tends to zero as the intensity $\lambda$ of the underlying Poisson point process tends to zero, for Poisson-Voronoi percolation defined on an ambient space from a family of geometric spaces that includes Cartesian products $\mathbb{H}^{d_1}\times\dots\times\mathbb{H}^{d_k}$ with $k,d_1,\dots,d_k\geq 2$. In contrast, for Poisson-Voronoi percolation on the hyperbolic plane $\mathbb{H}^2$, Benjamini and Schramm have shown that $p_u(\lambda)$ tends to one as $\lambda$ tends to zero, and $p_u(\lambda)>1/2$ for all $\lambda>0$. An unpublished argument of D'Achille and Curien shows that for Poisson-Voronoi percolation on $\mathbb{H}^d$ with $d\geq 3$, the uniqueness threshold satisfies $p_u(\lambda)\leq 1/2$ for all $\lambda>0$. Here we will show that $\inf_{\lambda>0}p_u(\lambda)>0$ for Poisson-Voronoi percolation on $\mathbb{H}^d$ with $d\geq 3$. This answers a question of Greb\'ik and Recke. The ideal Poisson-Voronoi tessellation is a random tessellation of $\mathbb{H}^d$ introduced recently by D'Achille et al. In a sense that can be made precise, it corresponds to the $\lambda\searrow 0$ limit of the Poisson-Voronoi tessellation. Via a minor adaptation of our proof, we are also able to show that the uniqueness threshold of the ideal Poisson-Voronoi tessellation is strictly positive.
item.dc:creator: Matthias Irlbeck, Tobias M\"uller

item.title: Multilevel limits of spiked random matrix corners processes
item.description: arXiv:2608.01531v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We consider the largest eigenvalues of submatrices of the classical Gaussian random matrices with a finite rank spike in the critical BBP regime. We show that they converge to a multilevel interlacing particle system whose lowest level is the Airy$_\beta$ point process. Our construction and scaling limits extend in a natural way to non-classical $\beta >0$.
item.dc:creator: Benjamin Landon, Tara Stojimirovic

item.title: Joint Laws of Maximum Drawdown and Maximum Drawup for Spectrally Negative L\'evy Processes
item.description: arXiv:2609.03634v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Let X be a spectrally negative L\'evy process observed up to an inde- pendent exponential time T with parameter {\gamma} > 0. We study the joint law of the maximum drawdown and the maximum drawup of X on [0, T ]. The path is decomposed according to the two possible orderings of its in- fimum and supremum. Conditional on the values of these extrema and on their ordering, the resulting pre-, intermediate, and post- components are independent. We identify their laws as Doob h-transforms of killed spec- trally negative L\'evy processes and express the corresponding distribution functions explicitly in terms of the {\gamma}-scale functions W ({\gamma}) and Z({\gamma}) and their derivatives. Combining the conditional laws with the joint densities of the extrema yields integral representations of the joint distribution and moments.
item.dc:creator: Ceren Vardar Acar, Emre Akdogan

item.title: Bulk-edge sticking beyond the Perron mode in Gaussian softmax attention
item.description: arXiv:2609.23949v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study row-softmax self-attention with independent Gaussian query and key weights in the proportional regime, at fixed inverse temperature. Hayase, Collins, and Karakida proved Gaussian equivalence for the empirical squared singular-value distribution after removal of the Perron direction. A global law alone does not exclude finitely many nonleading outliers. We prove that no such outliers persist: the rescaled squared singular value $\ell s_k(A)^2$ converges in probability to the upper edge of their bulk law for every fixed $k\ge 2$. In fact, this convergence is uniform over any deterministic sublinear number of leading non-Perron indices. The proof uses an exact decomposition of the softmax normalization, conditions on the key matrix, identifies the conditional covariance exactly with a diagonally conjugated inner-product kernel, linearizes that kernel in operator norm, and applies the outside-support local law of Fan, Ma, Paquette, and Wang. A separate stability argument identifies the finite conditional deformed Marchenko-Pastur edge with the limiting bulk edge. We also derive a scalar formula for that edge throughout the proportional regime and recover the explicit square-model formula of Hayase, Collins, and Karakida, including its physical branch.
item.dc:creator: Alexander Jerschow

item.title: Boolean threshold functions, neuron capacity, and memory retrieval
item.description: arXiv:2609.29756v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: How much information can a single neuron remember? How many memories can neural networks retrieve without creating false memories? These questions are related to a basic question: how many Boolean threshold functions $f(x)=\operatorname{sgn}(a_0+\langle a,x\rangle)$, $x\in\{-1,1\}^n$, are there? In this paper, we show that the number $T_n$ of distinct Boolean threshold functions is \[ T_n=2\binom{2^n-1}{n}\bigl(1+O(n^{-99})\bigr). \] Equivalently, the capacity of a single threshold neuron is $n^2-\log_2(n!)+1+O(n^{-99})$ bits, improving the $O(n)$ error term in the result of Kahn--Koml\'os--Szemer\'edi to $O(n^{-99})$. To prove this, we show that, for $1\le r\le n-1$, and $v_1,\ldots,v_r$ are chosen at random from $\{-1,1\}^n$, \[ \mathbb P\!\left\{ \langle v_1,\ldots,v_r\rangle\cap\{-1,1\}^n =\{\pm v_1,\ldots,\pm v_r\} \right\} =1-O(n^{-99}). \] In the context of the Kanter--Sompolinsky Hamiltonian for memory retrieval, this identifies $r=n-1$ as a sharp threshold, at which, for almost every collection of $r$ memories, the only ground states are these memories and their negatives, confirming a weaker form of the Kalai--Linial--Odlyzko conjecture. It also settles a recent open problem posed by M. Anthony on the specification number of Boolean threshold functions. In addition, we show that, for every $1\le r\le n-1$, \[ \mathbb P\{v_1,\ldots,v_r\text{ are linearly dependent}\} =2\binom r2\,2^{-n}+O\!\left(2^{-n}e^{-cn}\right), \] confirming a conjecture of Kahn--Koml\'os--Szemer\'edi.
item.dc:creator: Xinyuan Xie

item.title: A New Modifications of the Milstein and Euler Methods and the Taylor-Ito Expansion for Ito Stochastic Differential Equations with Drift and Diffusion Coefficients Having Non-Differentiable or Singular Time-Dependent Multipliers
item.description: arXiv:2610.29206v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The article presents a new modifications of the Milstein and Euler methods for systems of Ito stochastic differential equations with drift and diffusion coefficients having differentiable and non-differentiable or singular power-law time-dependent components (the latter depending only on the time variable). By iteratively applying Ito's formula to the mentioned differentiable components of the drift and diffusion coefficients, a new modification of the Milstein method is derived in the paper. A key feature of this modification of the Milstein method is the presence of time-dependent weight functions in the iterated Ito stochastic integrals of the second and first multiplicity (the specified weight functions are identically equal to unity in the classical Milstein method). To approximate the specified iterated Ito stochastic integrals (with respect to the components of a multidimensional Wiener process) that involve time-dependent weight functions, the paper proposes using the method of generalized multiple Fourier series, introduced by the first author in 2006. The article also provides a modification of the Euler method and the Taylor-Ito expansion for Ito SDEs with non-differentiable or singular drift and diffusion coefficients. The convergence rates of the proposed modifications of the Milstein and Euler methods are established. A series of numerical experiments has been performed to confirm the theoretical results of this paper.
item.dc:creator: Dmitriy F. Kuznetsov, Mikhail D. Kuznetsov

item.title: Ornstein--Uhlenbeck spirals: Absorption Probabilities and Conic Intrinsic Volumes
item.description: arXiv:2610.37911v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Let $(U_t)_{t\in\mathbb R}$ be a stationary Ornstein--Uhlenbeck process in $\mathbb R^d$ whose coordinate processes $(U_t^{(i)})_{t\in\mathbb R}$, $1\le i\le d$, are independent, centered, and have covariance function $\mathbb E [U_s^{(i)}U_t^{(i)}]=e^{-|t-s|/2}$. For every $T>0$, we obtain an explicit formula for the probability that the convex hull $\mathrm{conv}\{U_t:0\le t\le T\}$ contains the origin. We obtain a similar formula for a circular Ornstein--Uhlenbeck loop whose covariance is the normalized $T$-periodization of this kernel. For each fixed dimension $d$, we determine the precise long-time asymptotics of the non-absorption probabilities, which decay as explicit constants times $T^{d-1} e^{-T/2}$ as $T\to\infty$. We also show that, as $d\to\infty$, the absorption probabilities in both models undergo a transition from $0$ to $1$ around $T=2d$, with a common Gaussian limiting profile on the scale $\sqrt d$. We also obtain explicit formulas for the probability that $\sigma Z$ belongs to the convex hull of Brownian motion or Brownian bridge on $[0,1]$ in $\mathbb R^d$, where $Z$ is an independent standard Gaussian vector and $\sigma\ge0$. The large-$\sigma$ asymptotics recover the known formulas for the expected volumes of these convex hulls. Finally, we compute the conic intrinsic volumes of the closed positive hulls of deterministic Ornstein--Uhlenbeck spirals and their circular analogues in Hilbert spaces. Their Grassmann angles coincide with the corresponding Ornstein--Uhlenbeck absorption probabilities. After suitable rescaling, the small-time limits of these conic intrinsic volumes recover the formulas of Gao--Vitale and Gao for the intrinsic volumes of the Brownian body and its Brownian-bridge analogue.
item.dc:creator: Zakhar Kabluchko

item.title: Exponential Convergence of the Lifted Gradient Flow of the Bass Functional
item.description: arXiv:2610.40404v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: How quickly can we construct the martingale with prescribed initial and terminal laws that is closest to Brownian motion in the sense of the martingale Benamou-Brenier problem? The construction requires the initial law of an auxiliary Brownian motion. One can take this law to be the distribution of a minimizer of the lifted Bass functional. In dimension one, Backhoff, Pammer and Schachermayer proved, under additional assumptions, that the gradient flow of this functional converges exponentially to a minimizer. We extend this result to arbitrary dimension. Under the assumptions of the paper, the gradient flow starting from a bounded random vector converges exponentially in $L^2$ to the minimizer with the same mean. We prove this by showing that, for a fixed random vector $X$ with the prescribed initial law, the lifted Bass functional is strongly convex on each set of $\sigma(X)$-measurable vectors with a prescribed mean and a common $L^\infty$ bound.
item.dc:creator: Danila Litvinov (Faculty of Mathematics, HSE University)

item.title: Quantitative non-Gaussian and Gaussian approximation for exponential random graphs in the single-phase critical regime
item.description: arXiv:2611.05318v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We establish quantitative non-Gaussian and Gaussian approximations for edge-count fluctuations in dense exponential random graphs at single-phase criticality of any fixed even order $2m_*\ge 4$. The Hamiltonians use injective homomorphism counts of fixed simple graphs, with nonnegative leading coefficients for the higher-order terms. In bounded calibrated windows, edge-density fluctuations on the scale $n^{-1/m_*}$ admit an explicit non-Gaussian approximation with error $O(n^{-1/m_*})$. For parameter perturbations by fixed multiples of $n^{-1}$ with a nonzero first-order drift correction at the critical density, the deterministically centered edge count admits a Gaussian approximation on the scale $n^{(3m_*-2)/(2m_*-1)}$, with error $O(n^{-1/(2m_*-1)})$. Both rates hold in Wasserstein and Kolmogorov distances. The key step is to construct auxiliary kernels for exterior graphs outside an event of exponentially small probability. These kernels contract uniformly on the full row state space and agree with the conditional Gibbs updates on typical row configurations, yielding the conditional cumulant estimates used in Stein's method.
item.dc:creator: Ji-Shuai Miao, Yi-Kun Zhao

item.title: The Cost of Minimal Completeness: Gamma-to-Delta Aliasing in Discrete Markets
item.description: arXiv:2611.06692v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In one dimension, the symmetric binomial tree replicates quadratic payoffs using the Delta of its own price function. For every $d\geq 2$ and every centered, isotropic, minimally complete $(d+1)$-state model with $d$ risky assets, by contrast, some quadratic payoff requires a replicating hedge different from that Delta. In this nonredundant finite-state setting, centered one-step payoffs are spanned by the $d$ asset innovations; centered second-order (Gamma) contributions are therefore represented as first-order trading gains, potentially inducing additional asset holdings. We call this effect Gamma-to-Delta aliasing and measure it by the linear operator $\mathcal{A}_\xi(H)=\mathbb{E}[(\xi^\top H\xi-\operatorname{tr}H)\xi]$, where $\xi$ is the normalized one-step innovation and $H$ the Gamma matrix. For quadratic claims the replicating holding exceeds the price Delta by exactly $\sqrt{h}\,\mathcal{A}_\xi(H)/2$, where $h$ is the time step. Trading this holding in a Brownian market adds the tracking-error variance $hT|\mathcal{A}_\xi(H)|^2/4$, a fixed multiple of the ordinary discrete-Delta error that does not vanish in relative terms as $h\downarrow0$. We prove that the smallest worst-case aliasing over all minimally complete models is $\sqrt{d-1}$, so the worst-case relative excess variance is $(d-1)/2$; both are attained uniquely by the equal-probability regular simplex. For unit-Frobenius positive-semidefinite Gammas and for unit rank-one Gammas, the sharp minimax value is $(d-1)/\sqrt{d}$, with the same unique optimizer. We also show how aliasing trades off against unhedgeable quadratic risk when more states are allowed, and derive the leading implementation cost for smooth claims.
item.dc:creator: Akihiro Tanaka

item.title: Stochastic homogenization of $p$-resistance forms on nested fractals
item.description: arXiv:2611.13724v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study the stochastic homogenization of $p$-energies on infinite nested fractals. We assign i.i.d. random $p$-resistance forms $D_{0,\alpha}$ to level-$0$ cells of an infinite pre-nested fractal, and study the scaling limit of the resulting random $p$-resistance form $\mathcal{D}^{(0)}$. Under a moment condition on the reciprocal of $D_{0,\alpha}$, we prove that the sequence of rescaled and renormalized random energies is almost surely Mosco convergent to an equally weighted self-similar $p$-resistance form. As an application, when $p=2$, we prove the almost sure weak convergence of the associated rescaled continuous-time random walk. In particular, we allow arbitrarily small random conductances and impose no condition on the upper bound of random conductances.
item.dc:creator: Shiping Cao, Haiping Jiao, Hua Qiu

item.title: The bias interval of the elephant random walk
item.description: arXiv:2611.14576v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Gu\'erin, Laulin, Raschel, and Simon conjectured that the initial biases giving the superdiffusive elephant random walk a bimodal limit law form an interval centered at one half, and they described the problem as challenging. We prove this. For every superdiffusive memory the limit density has two local maxima exactly when the bias lies in a proper open interval, and outside it, including its endpoints, the density has a unique local maximum. The interval is nonempty exactly above a single memory threshold, numerically about $0.6688$. Near this threshold $a_*$ the distance between the two modes is of order $(a-a_*)^{1/2}$, and the width of the interval is of order $(a-a_*)^{3/2}$. The bias boundary is continuous and tends to zero at least quadratically fast as memory tends to one. The proof bounds the sign changes of the first and second differences of the finite walk, including those created at the boundary, and passes them to the limit.
item.dc:creator: Arjun Pemmasani

item.title: Averaging Principle and Uniform Large Deviations for Time-Dependent Slow-Fast Systems via Young-Rough Integration
item.description: arXiv:2611.16762v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The main aim of this work is to investigate the limiting behavior and asymptotic properties of time-dependent slow-fast stochastic dynamical systems. The slow component is driven by a stochastic process with H\"older-continuous paths of regularity greater than 1/2, while the fast component is driven by a Brownian rough path. We introduce a novel Young-rough integration framework tailored to such systems and establish well-posedness results, providing the analytical foundation for further asymptotic analysis. Building on this framework, we employ Khasminskii's time-discretization method to establish the strong convergence of the slow component to the solution of the corresponding averaged equation in the L^p-sense. Furthermore, when the driving noise in the slow equation is specified as a fractional Brownian motion, we apply the weak convergence approach to establish a uniform large deviation principle for the slow component, uniformly over compact sets of initial conditions, in the H\"older topology.
item.dc:creator: Wenting Xu

item.title: Ergodicity without monotonicity: patch-positive spin systems
item.description: arXiv:2611.17861v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Monotonicity is the standard tool for proving that an interacting particle system is ergodic. What can replace it when the system is not monotone and its invariant measure is unknown? The simplest such systems are kinetically constrained models such as FA-1f and East exposed to noise. In these models vacancies enable updates, so adding vacancies should help the system forget its initial state. We prove this for a broad class of spin systems, which we call patch-positive. If vacancies are created spontaneously at a uniformly positive rate, the system converges to the same equilibrium from a large class of initial states, and from every initial state if the threshold density is at most $\tfrac12$ or the interactions are oriented. In particular, the East model with noise is ergodic at every density, and we obtain new cases of the positive-rates conjecture. The key idea is to compare the dual processes of the system with and without the added deaths.
item.dc:creator: Maciej G{\l}uchowski, Georg Menz

item.title: The Rate of Convergence of Empirical $(p,q)$-Gromov-Wasserstein Distances
item.dc:creator: Pui Kuen Leung, Riku Okada, Samuel Lok-Hei Wong

item.title: Longest run for $q$-binary trials
item.description: arXiv:2611.27828v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We investigate the longest-run distribution for binary trials in which the success probability varies geometrically. Exact formulae are derived for the probability mass function and the cumulative distribution function of the length of the longest success run in a sequence of $q$-binary trials, using enumerative combinatorics. The setting covers independent but not necessarily identically distributed zero--one trials whose success probabilities follow a geometric rule, and the classical independent and identically distributed Bernoulli longest-run distribution is recovered in the limit $q\to 1$. A simulation study confirms accurate maximum likelihood estimation of the base success probability and the geometric parameter $q$, a well-calibrated and powerful boundary-corrected likelihood ratio test of the hypothesis that $q=1$, and close agreement between the analytical cumulative distribution function and its empirical counterpart.
item.dc:creator: Jungtaek Oh, Nurzhan Sapargali

item.title: Local Statistics of Random Permutations from Free Products
item.description: arXiv:2203.12250v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Let $\alpha$ and $\beta$ be uniformly random permutations of orders $2$ and $3$, respectively, in $S_{N}$, and consider, say, the permutation $\alpha\beta\alpha\beta^{-1}$. How many fixed points does this random permutation have on average? The current paper studies questions of this kind and relates them to surprising topological and algebraic invariants of elements in free products of groups. Formally, let $\Gamma=G_{1}*\ldots*G_{k}$ be a free product of groups where each of $G_1,\ldots,G_k$ is either finite, finitely generated free, or an orientable hyperbolic surface group. For a fixed element $\gamma\in\Gamma$, a $\gamma$-random permutation in the symmetric group $S_{N}$ is the image of $\gamma$ through a uniformly random homomorphism $\Gamma\to S_{N}$. In this paper we study local statistics of $\gamma$-random permutations and their asymptotics as $N$ grows. We first consider $\mathbb{E}\left[\mathrm{fix}_{\gamma}\left(N\right)\right]$, the expected number of fixed points in a $\gamma$-random permutation in $S_{N}$. We show that unless $\gamma$ has finite order, the limit of $\mathbb{E}\left[\mathrm{fix}_{\gamma}\left(N\right)\right]$ as $N\to\infty$ is an integer, and is equal to the number of subgroups $H\le\Gamma$ containing $\gamma$ such that $H\cong\mathbb{Z}$ or $H\cong C_{2}*C_{2}$. Equivalently, this is the number of subgroups $H\le\Gamma$ containing $\gamma$ and having (rational) Euler characteristic zero. We also prove there is an asymptotic expansion for $\mathbb{E}\left[\mathrm{fix}_{\gamma}\left(N\right)\right]$ and determine the limit distribution of the number of fixed points as $N\to\infty$. These results are then generalized to all statistics of cycles of fixed lengths.
item.dc:creator: Doron Puder, Tomer Zimhoni

item.title: Operator dependent para-controlled calculus, periodic homogenisation and singular PDEs
item.description: arXiv:2404.16320v4 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We develop a variant of the para-controlled distributions framework based on operator dependent (generalised) Besov spaces. This in particular covers the class of oscillatory operators from periodic homogenisation. We then apply the framework to study periodic homogenisation problems for a class of singular stochastic PDEs. One novel viewpoint is to measure regularity via the geometry induced by the operators at hand rather than classical Fourier basis. The generalised Besov spaces were introduced by Kerkyacharian-Petrushev. In contrast to the Fourier decomposition in the classical setting, they are built from spectral decomposition of general self-adjoint elliptic operators. A major difference is that products of two spectrally localised functions in general have ``frequencies" spread over the whole spectrum. We obtain a decay estimate on ``high frequency" component of the product of two spectrally-localised functions. This enables us to obtain uniform bounds for the naturally associated para-product and commutator operations over a class of operators. This in particular includes the family of periodic homogenisation operators uniform in the oscillation parameter. Next, we show convergence properties of these operations in the periodic homogenisation setting. A key ingredient is a sharp quantitative convergence of the generalised Littlewood-Paley block operators. The proof utilises the Helffer-Sj\"ostrand's formula for self-adjoint operators. Finally, we apply this framework to periodic homogenisation problems for dynamical $\phi^4_3$, $2$D gPAM, and $1$D KPZ. Assuming the convergence of stochastic objects to their homogenised limits, we show that the solutions and fluxes also converge to the corresponding limits. The convergence of the explicit stochastic terms with suitable renormalisations will be treated in a separate note.
item.dc:creator: Yilin Chen, Weijun Xu

item.title: Mahler's problem and Turyn polynomials
item.description: arXiv:2405.08281v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Mahler's problem asks for the largest possible value of the Mahler measure, normalized by the $L_2$ norm, of a polynomial with $\pm1$ coefficients and large degree. We establish a new record value of approximately $0.951$ in this problem by analyzing certain Turyn polynomials, which are defined by cyclically shifting the coefficients of a Fekete polynomial by a prescribed amount. Recently, Klurman, Lamzouri, and Munsch established that the distribution of values over the unit circle of Fekete polynomials of large degree is effectively modeled by a particular random point process. We extend this analysis to the Turyn polynomials, and determine expressions for the asymptotic normalized Mahler measure of these polynomials, as well as for their normalized $L_q$ norms. We also describe a number of calculations on the corresponding random processes, which indicate that the Turyn polynomials where the shift is approximately $1/4$ of the length have Mahler measure exceeding $95\%$ of their $L_2$ norm. Further, we show that these asymptotic values are not disturbed by a small change to make polynomials having entirely $\pm1$ coefficients, which establishes the result on Mahler's problem. We also estimate that the limiting value of the normalized $L_1$ norm of these polynomials exceeds $0.977$, in connection with a question of Newman.
item.dc:creator: Michael J. Mossinghoff

item.title: Localisation for the second-order Beckmann problem: bimartingale couplings and leaf decompositions
item.description: arXiv:2502.05683v4 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We develop a second-order localisation theory for optimal transport based on leaf decompositions and bimartingale couplings, which impose martingale constraints in opposite directions on complementary orthogonal subspaces. It provides a second-order analogue of the classical decomposition of optimal transport into transport rays and monotone couplings: transport rays are replaced by the leaves of the $1$-Lipschitz derivative map $Du$ of an optimal dual potential $u\in C^{1,1}(\mathbb R^n)$, while monotone couplings are replaced by bimartingale couplings. We apply this framework to the three-marginal optimal transport problem introduced by Bolbotowski and Bouchitt\'e, whose relaxation is the second-order Beckmann problem. We characterise the existence of bimartingale couplings through a convex-concave order condition. This yields a generalisation of Strassen's theorem from convex order to the convex-concave setting. Equivalently, the dual problem associated with the second-order Beckmann problem admits an optimiser whose derivative is an isometry. For absolutely continuous measures with common barycentre, assuming the existence of an optimal plan with absolutely continuous third marginal, we prove that every optimal plan decomposes into a family of problems on the leaves of $Du$. On each leaf, all optimal plans are completely described by bimartingale couplings between the corresponding conditional measures. Without this absolute continuity assumption on the third marginal, we show that the leaf decomposition persists in a more general form: optimal plans are mixtures of plans concentrated on triples $(x,y,z)$ satisfying $x\in \mathcal{S}_1$, $y\in \mathcal{S}_2$, and $z\in \mathcal{S}_1\cap \mathcal{S}_2$, where $\mathcal{S}_1$ and $\mathcal{S}_2$ are neighbouring leaves of $Du$.
item.dc:creator: Krzysztof J. Ciosmak

item.title: Strong convergence of uniformly random permutation representations of surface groups
item.description: arXiv:2504.08988v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Let $\Gamma$ be the fundamental group of a closed orientable surface of genus at least two. Consider the composition of a uniformly random element of $\mathrm{Hom}(\Gamma,S_n)$ with the $(n-1)$-dimensional irreducible representation of $S_n$. We prove the strong convergence in probability as $n\to\infty$ of this sequence of random representations to the regular representation of $\Gamma$. As a consequence, for any closed orientable hyperbolic surface $X$, with probability tending to one as $n\to\infty$, a uniformly random degree-$n$ covering space of $X$ has near optimal relative spectral gap --- ignoring the eigenvalues that arise from the base surface $X$. To do so, we show that the polynomial method of proving strong convergence can be extended beyond rational settings. To meet the requirements of this extension we prove two new kinds of results. First, we show there are effective polynomial approximations of expected values of traces of elements of $\Gamma$ under random homomorphisms to $S_{n}$. Secondly, we estimate the growth rates of probabilities that a finitely supported random walk on $\Gamma$ is a proper power after a given number of steps.
item.dc:creator: Michael Magee, Doron Puder, Ramon van Handel

item.title: Scheduling in Queueing Systems with Uncertain and Evolving Holding Costs
item.description: arXiv:2505.21331v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: In queueing systems, the holding costs of jobs may evolve in uncertain ways. For example, in content moderation for social media platforms, the cost of delaying the review of a content piece is proportional to its view trajectory, which fluctuates and is a priori unknown. To capture such uncertain and evolving holding cost patterns, we consider a queueing model where job states evolve based on a Markov chain with state-dependent instantaneous holding costs. We demonstrate that in the presence of such uncertain and evolving holding costs, the two canonical algorithmic principles, instantaneous-cost ($c\mu$-rule) and expected-remaining-cost ($c\mu/\theta$-rule), are suboptimal. By viewing each job as a Markovian ski-rental problem, we develop a new index-based algorithm, Opportunity-adjusted Remaining Cost (OaRC), that adjusts to the opportunity of serving jobs in the future when uncertainty partly resolves. We show that the suboptimality gap of OaRC scales as $\tilde{O}(\sqrt{N})$, where $N$ is the system size. This bound shows that OaRC achieves asymptotic optimality for overloaded systems when the system size $N$ scales to infinity. Moreover, the bound is independent of the state-space size, which is a desirable property when job states contain contextual information. We corroborate our results with an extensive simulation study based on two holding cost patterns (online ads and user-generated content) that arise in content moderation for social media platforms. Our simulations based on synthetic and real datasets demonstrate that OaRC consistently outperforms existing practice, which is based on the two canonical algorithmic principles.
item.dc:creator: Caner Gocmen, Thodoris Lykouris, Deeksha Sinha, Wentao Weng

item.title: Differential Equations for Macdonald's Hypergeometric Series
item.description: arXiv:2510.10875v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We study differential equations for certain multivariable hypergeometric series, introduced by Macdonald in the 1980s, which generalize hypergeometric functions of matrix argument due to Bochner and Herz. Such equations are well studied in the one-variable case, where they serve to characterize the classical hypergeometric functions $_p F_q(z)$ and provide a route to many of their key properties. Accordingly, Macdonald asked for a similar characterization for the multivariate series. This problem, however, has remained open. Differential equations are known only for a handful of cases with $p\leq 3$ and $q\leq 2$. In this paper we give a complete solution to Macdonald's problem. In the multivariable case there are \emph{two} series $_p F_q(x)$ and $_p F_q(x,y)$, depending on $p+q+1$ parameters and one or two sets of variables, $x=(x_1,\dots,x_n)$ and $y=(y_1,\dots,y_n)$. We give differential equations characterizing both series, for all values of $p$ and $q$. The proof involves several new ideas in the theory of symmetric functions, especially Jack polynomials and interpolation polynomials.
item.dc:creator: Hong Chen, Siddhartha Sahi

item.title: Random-Bridges as Stochastic Transports for Generative Models
item.description: arXiv:2512.14190v5 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: This paper motivates the use of random-bridges -- stochastic processes conditioned to take target distributions at fixed timepoints -- in the realm of generative modelling. Herein, random-bridges act as stochastic transports between two probability distributions when appropriately initialized, displaying either Markovian or non-Markovian, and continuous, discontinuous, or hybrid patterns depending on the choice of the driving process. We show how one can start from general probabilistic statements and branch out into specific representations for learning and simulation algorithms. Essentially, our framework formulates stochastic transports as noisy information processes governing the dynamic translation and propagation of information between arbitrary probability measures. Our theoretical and algorithmic presentation details training and simulation frameworks for both Gaussian and L\'evy (specifically, Gamma, Poisson and Stable-$1/2$) random-bridge transports. The empirical validation focuses on the Gaussian case for demonstration and comparison purposes, where our construct delivers high-quality samples, achieving competitive Fr\'echet Inception Distance scores compared to widely used denoising diffusions and flow matching frameworks.
item.dc:creator: Stefano Goria, Levent A. Meng\"ut\"urk, Murat C. Meng\"ut\"urk, Berkan Sesen

item.title: Kantorovich Distance via Spanning Trees: Properties and Algorithms
item.description: arXiv:2601.08396v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We study optimal transport between probability measures supported on the same finite metric space, where the ground cost is a distance induced by a weighted connected graph. Building on recent work showing that the resulting Kantorovich distance can be expressed as a minimization problem over the set of spanning trees of this underlying graph, we investigate the implications of this reformulation on the construction of an optimal transport plan and a dual potential based on the solution of such an optimization problem. In this setting, we derive an explicit formula for the Kantorovich potential in terms of the imbalanced cumulative mass (a generalization of the cumulative distribution in R) along an optimal spanning tree solving such a minimization problem, under a weak non-degeneracy condition on the pair of measures that guarantees the uniqueness of a dual potential. Our second contribution establishes the existence of an optimal transport plan that can be computed efficiently by a dynamic programming procedure once an optimal spanning tree is known. Finally, we propose a stochastic algorithm based on simulated annealing on the space of spanning trees to compute such an optimal spanning tree. Numerical experiments illustrate the theoretical results and demonstrate the practical relevance of the proposed approach for optimal transport on finite metric spaces.
item.dc:creator: J\'er\'emie Bigot, Luis Fredes

item.title: Well-Conditioned Oblivious Perturbations in Linear Space
item.description: arXiv:2604.23193v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Perturbing a deterministic $n$-dimensional matrix with small Gaussian noise is a cornerstone of smoothed analysis of algorithms [Spielman and Teng, JACM 2004], as it reduces the condition number of the input to $O(n)$, and with it the complexity of many matrix algorithms. However, when deployed algorithmically, these perturbations are expensive due to the cost of generating and storing $n^2$ Gaussian random variables. We propose a perturbation that requires generating and storing $O(n)$ random numbers in $O(\log n)$ bits of precision, and reduces the condition number of any deterministic matrix to $O(n)$, matching Gaussian perturbations. Our result takes a step towards derandomizing matrix perturbations in numerical linear algebra, and in particular, implies that we can solve an $n\times n$ linear system to within $\varepsilon$ backward error in $O(n^2\log(n)/\varepsilon)$ time using only $O(n\log n)$ random bits. In our construction, we introduce the concept of a pattern matrix, which is a dense deterministic matrix that maps all sparse vectors into dense vectors in a way that goes beyond the classical uncertainty principle of the Fourier transform. We combine this with a sparse perturbation whose entries are dependent and located in a non-uniform fashion. In order to analyze this construction, we develop new techniques for lower bounding the smallest singular value of a random matrix with dependent entries.
item.dc:creator: Shabarish Chenakkod, Micha{\l} Derezi\'nski, Xiaoyu Dong, Mark Rudelson

item.title: Structural and Lagrangian properties of analogue ensembles to characterize multifractality of stochastic processes
item.description: arXiv:2605.08155v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We present a framework for the scale-invariance characterization of stochastic processes in reconstructed finite-dimensional spaces. This framework analyses the structural and dynamical properties of the reconstructed space and is based on a Takens embedding reconstruction followed by the definition of ensembles of analogue states. First, we specify a collection of target states densely sampling the full embedding space. For each target state, we search for the ensemble of its k-nearest neighbors, its k-best analogues, and we analyze its volume and dynamics. On the one hand, we study the probability distribution of the volumes and relate its mean and variance to the scale-invariance properties of the stochastic process. On the second hand, we study the Lagrangian properties of the analogues by characterizing how they disperse in time. More particularly, we study the volume occupied by the analogue's successors in function of time and of their initial volume. The main contribution of this paper is to highlight the link between these dynamical properties and the scale-invariance features of the process. We analyze two types of stationary and dissipative 1-dimensional scale-invariant processes: regularized fractional Brownian motion and regularized multifractal random walk. For both processes, the structure and dynamics of the embedding space are determined by their scale-invariant properties.
item.dc:creator: Carlos Granero-Belinchon (ODYSSEY, IMT Atlantique - MEE, Lab-STICC\_OSE)

item.title: A tree-like fractal Dirichlet space lying between strong and weak elliptic Harnack inequalities
item.description: arXiv:2605.15479v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: In this paper we construct a self-similar fractal configured as an infinitely branched tree and equip it with a regular self-similar Dirichlet form. Fixing a typical metric ball, we compute accurately the effective resistance between an inner point and the boundary of this ball. Based on this result, anomalous behaviour of the mean exit time from such balls is shown -- the ratio between whose supremum and infimum can be arbitrarily large. Under properly selected self-similar measure, we further show the weak elliptic Harnack inequality holds but the strong analogue fails.
item.dc:creator: Caoxu Huang, Guanhua Liu

item.title: A Gallager-Type Redundancy Bound for Binary Fano Coding
item.description: arXiv:2607.04192v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Binary Fano codes build a complete prefix code by repeatedly splitting the sorted list of symbol probabilities into two halves whose total probabilities are as close to each other as possible. Kraj\v{c}i, Liu, Mike\v{s}, and Moser proved in 2015 that the redundancy $R$ of this code satisfies $R\le1-p_n$, where $p_n$ is the smallest symbol probability. We prove that $R<U(p_1)$, where $U$ is a piecewise function of the largest symbol probability $p_1$ with $U<1$. In particular, $R<p_1+4-\tfrac53\log_2 5$ for every source, and $R<\tfrac52-\tfrac56\log_2 5$ when $p_1<\tfrac12$. The bound equals the supremum of the redundancy for $p_1\ge\tfrac12$ and on an interval just below $\tfrac13$, and we give a lower bound for the other values of $p_1$. Unlike the bounds for Huffman codes, the proofs do not use the sibling property. They work directly with the Fano split rule, mainly through the facts that every split is nearly balanced and that the redundancy is a sum of one term per internal node of the tree.
item.dc:creator: Kamila Szewczyk

item.title: Proper-Score Observation-Driven Filters: Tracking Efficiency, Estimation, and Continuous-Time Limits
item.description: arXiv:2608.02828v4 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Observation-driven filters usually update a time-varying parameter with the score of the predictive log density. Replacing the logarithmic score by another proper scoring rule changes both the target the filter tracks and the precision with which it tracks it. These filters form a subclass of the PRADA models of de Punder (2026), and we study their properties at the level of the filtered path. In an in-fill framework, the local tracking error is an Ornstein--Uhlenbeck process. Optimised over the gain, its invariant variance is the geometric mean of the target's volatility and an effective observation noise determined by the scoring rule. Tracking efficiency is the squared correlation between the scoring-rule driver and the true score at the rule's own target. In scale models it equals the asymptotic relative efficiency of the corresponding static minimum-score estimator. The resulting frontier quantifies the robustness--efficiency trade-off. Under Gaussian innovations, density-power and CRPS volatility filters raise minimal tracking risk by 3% and 11%. Under Student-$t_5$ innovations, the Gaussian log-score filter raises it by 58% in the limit, and by more at daily frequency. We also give primitive conditions for bounded scale-invariant drivers, a matrix version, a population self-tuning result for the gain, minimum-score estimation theory whose invertibility conditions hold at the fitted values, and diffusion limits. An international equity application separates the roles of the predictive density and the scoring rule.
item.dc:creator: Giulia Livieri, Gianluca Palmari

item.title: Satellite Infrastructure Sharing: Orbit-Structured Stochastic Geometry Modeling and Connectivity Analysis in Heterogeneous Satellite Networks
item.description: arXiv:2608.12265v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: This paper develops an analytical framework to evaluate the feasibility and performance of satellite infrastructure sharing among multiple low Earth orbit (LEO) satellite operators. Motivated by the growing demand for universal connectivity under limited satellite resources, the proposed model captures uncoordinated deployments where independently operated constellations coexist without predefined orbital agreements. To describe such heterogeneous configurations, the spherical Cox point process is employed to jointly generate orbital structures and satellites. Then, each satellite is further assigned a random communication range, reflecting variations in coverage capability across operators. The overall coverage region is modeled through a spherical Cox-Boolean model that captures the spatial overlap of individual satellite spherical footprints on Earth. Using the proposed framework, the feasibility and benefits of satellite infrastructure sharing are mathematically analyzed, and closed-form expressions are derived for key performance metrics such as the connection probability, connection number, and downlink signal characteristics including the nearest serving distance, total received signal power, and the signal-to-interference ratio (SIR) distribution in the interference-limited regime. The analytical results, validated through system-level simulations, provide a tractable characterization of how orbital geometry governs coverage, connectivity, and interference, and reveal the inherent trade-offs induced by coverage overlap in heterogeneous satellite constellations.
item.dc:creator: Chang-Sik Choi

item.title: Fixed point properties for random groups in the density model with $d > \frac{1}{4}$
item.description: arXiv:2609.21255v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We prove that random groups in Gromov's density model have Kazhdan's property~\((T)\) asymptotically almost surely (a.a.s.) at every density \(d>\frac14\). Together with Ashcroft's theorem for \(d<\frac14\), this establishes \(\frac14\) as the sharp threshold and settles the long-standing problem of determining the threshold for property $(T)$ in the density model. More generally, for every fixed number of generators \(n\ge2\) and density \(d\in(\frac14,1)\), there exists \(C_{n,d}>0\) such that, a.a.s., every affine isometric action on a real \(L^p\)-space has a fixed point simultaneously for all \[ 1\le p\le C_{n,d}\sqrt{\frac{l}{\log l}}, \] where \(l\) is the relator length. In particular, \(\frac14\) is also the threshold for each fixed \(L^p\) fixed point property, \(1\le p<\infty\). We also establish a simultaneous fixed point theorem for a large class of uniformly smooth real Banach spaces with a common power-type convexity bound and a suitable common bound on their uniform curvature moduli. We further prove that, for each fixed real Banach space in a class that, to the best of our knowledge, contains all currently known examples of super-reflexive Banach spaces, random groups at density $d>1/4$ a.a.s.\ have the fixed point property for affine isometric actions. The proof combines a fixed point criterion based on harmonic cocycles with spectral estimates for random bipartite multigraphs arising from decompositions of relators into four consecutive subwords. All asymptotic conclusions hold as \(\RelLen\to\infty\) through all positive integers.
item.dc:creator: Izhar Oppenheim

item.title: A Wasserstein Trust-Region Method for Smooth Potential-Interaction Energies
item.description: arXiv:2610.08883v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Finding low-energy particle configurations and approximating probability distributions both lead to minimizing potential-interaction energies in Wasserstein space. Second-order information can speed up minimizing these possibly nonconvex energies, but a quadratic model is accurate only near the current measure. We introduce a Wasserstein trust-region (WTR) method for smooth, possibly nonconvex energies of this type. Each iteration transports the current measure $\rho$ along a displacement field $s$, producing $(\mathrm{Id}+s)_\#\rho$. The field approximately minimizes a quadratic model built from the second variation of the energy, subject to $\|s\|_{L^2(\rho)}\le\Delta$, using a truncated conjugate-gradient method. The ratio of actual to predicted decrease determines step acceptance and updates the trust-region radius. Under a lower energy bound and globally bounded Hessians of the potential and interaction kernel, we prove that the objective is nonincreasing, the Wasserstein-gradient norms converge to zero, and an $\varepsilon$-stationary iterate is reached within $O(\varepsilon^{-2})$ iterations, rejected ones included. If the potential is quadratically coercive, every weak accumulation point is stationary. For empirical measures, WTR is an ordinary trust-region method in the particle positions, and its complexity bound does not depend on the number of particles provided the initial energy exceeds its infimum by a bounded amount. For $2048$ and $4096$ particles with Gaussian pair repulsion in a two-dimensional harmonic trap, WTR reaches the gradient tolerance $2\times10^{-4}$ a median $1.40$ times faster than L-BFGS. For equal-weight integration rules on two non-Gaussian targets, WTR reaches an integration error of $10^{-4}$ about $1.8$ times faster than L-BFGS and $1.3$ times faster than a Krylov trust-region solver.
item.dc:creator: You Wan, Ting Gao, Jinqiao Duan, Jie Sun

item.title: Stochastic Gradient Leimkuhler-Matthews Integrator with Second Order Discretization Error
item.description: arXiv:2610.24781v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Stochastic gradient Langevin dynamics (SGLD) has a discretization error of first order in the step size $h$, even with the full gradient. We study the stochastic gradient Leimkuhler--Matthews (SGLM) integrator, which has the same cost as SGLD, one stochastic gradient per step, and reuses each Gaussian vector in consecutive steps. For a potential strongly convex outside a ball and a Lipschitz test function, we prove the bound $\mathcal O(\frac{1}{Nh} + \Sigma^2 h^2 + h^4 \log^2\frac1h)$ on the mean square error (MSE) of time averages of SGLM over $N$ steps, where $\Sigma$ bounds the variance of the gradient noise. The proof uses a modified class that absorbs the non-Markovian part of SGLM. The discretization error enters this bound as $h^4 \log^2\frac1h$ and the MSE bound of SGLD as $h^2$, while a larger batch reduces only the term $\Sigma^2 h^2$ in both bounds. In Bayesian logistic regression on MNIST, SGLM has a smaller estimated MSE than SGLD. The coefficient of $h$ in the numerical bias of SGLM is given explicitly by the covariance of the gradient noise and the continuous Poisson equation. The coefficient for SGLD contains in addition the Hessian of the potential, which comes from the discretization error.
item.dc:creator: Xuda Ye, Yuliang Wang, Guang Lin, Cindy Xiangrui Kong

item.title: Bayesian Inference in Partially Observed Critical Systems
item.description: arXiv:2610.35973v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We ask how much of a large random system must be observed to infer a global average with controlled uncertainty. For the random transposition shuffle, a conjugate Bayesian estimator of the average displacement, computed from $m$ sampled cards, has relative uncertainty $1/\sqrt{2m}$, independent of the deck size $n$. Because the configuration is a single draw from equilibrium, a floor $R_n$ remains, and no relative tolerance below $\kappa\sqrt{R_n}$ can be certified, even by a census. For the shuffle $R_n=(2n^2+7)/\bigl(5(n-1)^2(n+1)\bigr)$. Before equilibrium, a certificate built on the displacement loses sight after about $\frac n4\ln m$ steps, half as long as the count of fixed cards in the same sample. At the two-dimensional Ising critical point the floor of the energy vanishes, whereas that of the magnetisation stays near $0.072$, with mean-field limit $\sqrt2-1$. For correlated fields, the usual 95\% interval can cover the ensemble mean in only 7\% of cases, and no bound on the floor from one realisation holds under stationarity alone.
item.dc:creator: Mihika Singhania

item.title: On the Conditional Consistency of the Bootstrap
item.description: arXiv:2611.02243v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: This paper focuses on the conditional consistency of the bootstrap. The target is the conditional law of a statistic given a common shock, and the bootstrap approximates it by the law of a resampled statistic conditional on the shock and the data. We call the bootstrap consistent if these laws are close in the Kolmogorov distance for almost every realization of the shock. The conditioning $\sigma$-algebras are allowed to be unrelated across sample sizes, and both the comparison law and the dimension of the data may vary with the sample size. We give sufficient conditions for consistency in this sense, show that they yield asymptotically correct conditional coverage for bootstrap quantiles, and provide a finite-sample bound on the coverage error. We also relate the Kolmogorov formulation to the merging of probability measures. The results are specialized to statistics depending smoothly on an estimator or on an estimated nuisance parameter.
item.dc:creator: Denis Kojevnikov

item.title: Beyond weak convergence of signed spectral measures: Eigenvector overlaps and high-dimensional prediction risk
item.description: arXiv:2611.14836v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Many results in random matrix theory and high-dimensional statistics depend on weak convergence of spectral measures, which is usually established via pointwise convergence of Stieltjes transforms. This approach has recently been applied to signed measures. However, for signed measures, pointwise convergence of Stieltjes transforms alone no longer characterizes weak convergence. While this is unproblematic in many cases, in the high-dimensional regression setting, recently considered by Green and Romanov, the underlying signed eigenvector-overlap measures can fail to converge weakly, despite pointwise convergence of their Stieltjes transforms. Using a novel approach to risk analysis, we show that weak convergence can be replaced by a simple convergence result for bilinear forms. This allows us to establish convergence of the prediction risk for estimators based on arbitrary continuous spectral filters, including (regularized) gradient descent and ridge regression, even when the underlying signed measures fail to converge weakly. Under additional regularity conditions, we construct an explicit finite signed measure yielding an integral representation of the asymptotic prediction risk. This representation provides necessary and sufficient conditions for minimum-norm interpolation and optimally tuned ridge regression to attain the smallest asymptotic prediction risk among estimators with continuous spectral filters. Moreover, we provide characterizations of weak and vague convergence of finite signed measures in terms of pointwise convergence of their Stieltjes transforms.
item.dc:creator: Thomas Stark, Georg K\"ostenberger, Nina D\"ornemann

item.title: Convergence rate of periodic homogenization for Hamilton--Jacobi equations with supercritical viscosity
item.description: arXiv:2611.20638v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: This paper is devoted to studying the convergence rate in periodic homogenization of the viscous Hamilton--Jacobi equation (with supercritical viscosity index $\sigma>1$) \[ \partial_t u_\varepsilon+H(x/\varepsilon,\partial_xu_\varepsilon)=\varepsilon^\sigma\Delta u_\varepsilon,\quad (x,t)\in\mathbb{R}^n\times\mathbb{R}_+,\ \] subject to a given initial datum. For Tonelli Hamiltonians $H$, the solution $u_\varepsilon$ is proved to converge to a certain $u:\mathbb{R}^n\times\mathbb{R}\rightarrow\mathbb{R}$ (solving the effective problem) in the optimal rate $O(\varepsilon^{\min\{\sigma-1,1\}})$. We also obtain a rate for the case of non-convex Hamiltonians and discussed its optimality therein.
item.dc:creator: Gengyu Liu, Zibo Wang, Jianlu Zhang

item.title: On the $\phi^4_2$ theory on $\mathbb R\times S$
item.description: arXiv:2611.23032v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We present a construction of the Euclidean two-dimensional $\phi^4$ quantum field theory model on $\mathbb R\times S$ using parabolic stochastic quantization and discuss the Osterwalder-Schrader axioms. Motivated by one-loop string scattering amplitudes, we first construct finite-volume measures on a family of tori with varying geometry. To construct an infinite-volume measure on the cylinder, we establish uniform renormalization and stochastic estimates as the complex structure varies, including the degenerating regime in which the torus approaches an infinite cylinder.
item.dc:creator: Azam Jahandideh
